title: Visit-ending ozone windows gave no clear moisture interaction difference in four eastern US forest samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We tested whether the ozone-by-soil-moisture slope for visible leaf injury changes when ozone exposure ends on the field visit day. We used 5,906 matched site-year records from two eastern US forest regions and two periods in 1994-2010. Each exposure was scaled by its within-site standard deviation. Models controlled site, year, visit day, temperature, manual version, plant count and species count. Paired slope differences ranged from -0.364 to +0.218 percentage points of injury probability per ozone SD and moisture SD. All four state-cluster intervals included zero after correction for four tests. Site-only and closer-monitor checks also gave uncertain differences. This is a follow-up with records shared with a prior campaign study. The windows differ in length and monitor coverage. The visit-ending measure includes the visit day, and soil moisture can extend after the visit. The test does not isolate post-visit ozone or identify causal effects. Code, aggregate results, exact source hashes and an independent numerical check are included.

display.caption: Separate ozone-by-moisture slopes and their paired differences in four matched forest samples. Each interval uses a four-test correction. Ozone is scaled by each window's within-site SD. The models control site, year, visit conditions and measured effort.

citations.reason: Uses the verified panel and reviews exposure code. Adds matched regional and period window contrasts with paired state-cluster uncertainty. Records overlap; this is not independent source validation.
